n=512 b640 dense path: the FP16 blocked-Householder runs at only ~34 of ~960 TF32 TFLOP/s, with the trailing-reflector apply (qr_panel_apply_fused) eating 50.8% of GPU time. Replace it with a CholeskyQR + Householder-reconstruction (ORHR_COL) pipeline that is ~all tensor-core GEMM: form Gram G=A^T A via 3xTF32 SYRK, Cholesky+TRSM for explicit Q (shifted first pass s=11{mn+n(n+1)}u*||A||^2 then a 2nd CholeskyQR pass for O(u) orthogonality), then reconstruct the exact compact (H,tau) by a modified-LU of (Q-S) per LAPACK ?orhr_col (S_ii=-sgn of the LU pivot; v below-diag = q/(q_ii+sgn); tau from reconstructed V; R_out=S*R_in). Guard: if the Gram Cholesky fails (kappa overflow) fall back to the current FP16 path so the correctness gate is never violated. Aim to beat 3332us on shape 3.

PyTorch shifted-CholeskyQR2 + orhr_col (tau-override) wired into n=512 B>=120 dispatch via _scqr2_n512, reusing the batched recon_lu_cpp/build_H_inplace + tri_solve_right_inv C++ kernels. All 22 TEST shapes pass (n512 tests are B=16 -> small-batch geqrf path), but the diff_correctness_guard at B=640 with --seq reseeding FAILS: rankdef 2/8 and clustered 1/8 wrong. Root cause: sCQR2 is applied to the WHOLE n512 batch incl ill-conditioned rankdef/clustered/nearrank/mixed, and the per-matrix geqrf good-gate fallback misses some reseeded ill-cond members. FIX next: gate sCQR2 to ONLY the well-conditioned dense batch; route ill-cond to the existing qr_n512_mixed_driver.

Gated sCQR2 to dense-only (all-good gate; ill-cond batches decline and route to the proven qr_n512_mixed_driver -> all guards CLEAN). Enabled TF32 matmul (was SIMT FP32 sgemm, 30x slower) and switched the right-TRSM block to nb=64 (was 512 -> one giant SIMT batched-trsm). shape3 43502->28592us. STILL 8.5x slower than baseline (~3332): nsys shows the TWO batched cuSOLVER cholesky_ex calls (potrf_syrk/potrfBatch kernels) = ~26% of GPU time (~7.2ms), ~60x above the tensor-core floor (~120us). Next: replace cuSOLVER batched potrf with a custom blocked tensor-core Cholesky (warp 64x64 diag + cuBLAS panel TRSM + 3xTF32/FP16 SYRK trailing), batched over B=640.

Built a custom batched blocked tensor-core Cholesky (batched_chol_upper: warp 64x64 diag + fused panel solve + TF32 trailing GEMM, verified correct vs torch.cholesky via the diff guard) and a 3xTF32 batched Gram (gram_3xtf32). Both validate CLEAN. KEY FINDING via scqr2 debug trace: pass-1 (shifted) Cholesky succeeds (info1bad=0) but pass-2 Cholesky FAILS on 419/640 matrices -- G2=Q1^TQ1 is near-singular. Root cause: at cond(A)~1e5 the smallest eigenvalue of A^TA is smin^2~5e-8, but the Fukaya sCQR shift s~0.16 >> smin^2, so Q1=A R1^{-1} loses the small-column directions (Q1^TQ1 = I - s G1^{-1} has ~0 eigenvalues). Shifted CholeskyQR2 in FP32 only works for cond(A)<=1/sqrt(u)~4e3; the dense n512 shapes reach 1e5. Pivot: 1-pass CholeskyQR with an EXACT (FP64-accumulated) Gram + FP64 Cholesky + tau-override (the n4096 path's recipe), no shift. shape3 stuck ~27ms (sCQR2 declines->driver). geomean 3582.

Switched to 1-pass CholeskyQR with an EXACT FP64-accumulated Gram (A.double()^T A.double()) + FP64 cholesky_ex + 3xTF32 TRSM + orhr_col + tau-override (the n4096 recipe). VALID all guards. CORRECTNESS CONFIRMED: the dense n512 shape3 batch now ACCEPTS (Cholesky infobad=0, Q colnorm_dev_max=0.0072 << 5e-2 gate); ill-cond batches (mixed 103 bad, rankdef 640 bad, clustered colnorm 2.6e7) correctly decline to the FP16 driver. BUT shape3 is still ~25.4ms: nsys shows the FP64 Gram (cutlass d884gemm) = 4.84ms and the FP64 batched cholesky (potrf_syrk_nc<double> etc) = ~5ms dominate -- FP64 GEMM/chol run ~10-40 TFLOP/s on B200. The EXACT-Gram requirement (cond(G)~1e10, smin^2/smax^2~1e-10 below any TF32 floor) is real, so the path needs the Ozaki INT8 exact Gram + a fast FP64 blocked Cholesky to have any chance vs the 3.3ms baseline. geomean 3500.

FINAL CholeskyQR candidate: full pipeline = Ozaki INT8 exact Gram -> custom FP64 DMMA blocked Cholesky (batched_chol_upper_fp64, verified vs torch) -> 3xTF32 batched right-TRSM (Q=A R^-1) -> orhr_col recon (recon_lu_cpp+build_H_inplace) -> tau-override; plus a cheap col-norm-ratio pre-check that skips sCQR2 for ill-cond batches (->FP16 driver). VALID all guards. RESULT: dense shape3 = 21.5ms (~6.5x the FP16 baseline ~3.3ms); shapes 7/9/10 stay at driver speed via the pre-check (5368/3212/2506us); geomean 2109 vs baseline 1756 (REGRESSION, all from shape3). PROFILE (shape3): cost spread across Ozaki Gram ~14% (recombine bandwidth on the 5GB P buffer), FP64 Cholesky panel+diag+trailing ~21%, TRSM ~15%, recon ~10%. VERDICT: CholeskyQR+ORHR_COL does NOT beat the FP16 Householder for n512 cond2 -- cond(A) up to 1e5 (cond(G) up to 1e10, smin^2/smax^2~1e-10 below any TF32 floor) forces an EXACT Gram + FP64 Cholesky, and those FP64/Ozaki ops on B200 (~10-67 TFLOP/s vs ~960 TF32) cost ~6x the highly-tuned FP16 path. The brief's '~all tensor-core GEMM' premise fails because the conditioning forbids TF32 in the Gram/Cholesky.

BRIEF EXHAUSTED -- NEGATIVE VERDICT (committed, validated, regression). Built the full CholeskyQR+ORHR_COL pipeline for dense n512 in the live submission: Ozaki INT8 exact Gram -> custom FP64 DMMA blocked Cholesky (new batched_chol_upper_fp64 + an FP32 batched_chol_upper + gram_3xtf32, all verified correct vs torch via the reseeding diff guard) -> 3xTF32 batched right-TRSM (reused tri_solve_right_inv) -> orhr_col recon (reused recon_lu_cpp+build_H_inplace) -> tau-override; gated to the dense batch by a cheap col-norm-ratio pre-check + a post good-gate, ill-cond batches route to the proven FP16 mixed driver. ALL GUARDS PASS at every committed iter. RESULT: dense shape3 = 21.5ms vs the ~3.3ms FP16 baseline (~6.5x SLOWER); geomean 2109 vs baseline 1756 (regression entirely from shape3; shapes 7/9/10 held at driver speed by the pre-check). ROOT CAUSE (firm, measured): the dense n512 cond=2 batch has cond(A) up to ~1e5 (cond(G)~1e10, smin^2/smax^2~1e-10), BELOW any TF32 Gram's ~6e-8 floor -- proven by tracing: shifted-CQR2 in FP32 fails (pass-2 Cholesky non-PD on 419/640, the shift s~0.16 >> smin^2~5e-8), and a 3xTF32 Gram cannot resolve the small eigenvalues. So the path is forced into an EXACT Gram (Ozaki, ~3ms incl ~1.8ms recombine bandwidth on a 5GB P buffer) + an FP64 Cholesky (~4.5ms; DMMA/SIMT FP64 on B200 run ~10-67 TFLOP/s vs ~960 TF32). Those two alone (~7.5ms) exceed the whole FP16 baseline. The brief's '~all tensor-core GEMM' premise does not hold here because the conditioning forbids TF32 in the Gram and Cholesky; the FP16 blocked Householder is backward-stable (never squares cond) and stays far cheaper. RECOMMENDATION: do NOT pursue CholeskyQR for n512 cond2 -- the precision tax is fundamental. The reusable wins from this branch: batched_chol_upper_fp64 (FP64 DMMA blocked Cholesky, fully batched, ~2.4ms faster than cuSOLVER's SIMT potrf for B=640 n=512) and gram_3xtf32 -- these could help any FUTURE path that legitimately needs a fast batched FP64 Cholesky or 3xTF32 Gram. If the manager wants to keep attacking the n512 qr_panel_apply 50.8%, a better angle is optimizing the FP16 trailing apply itself (it is already a GEMM) rather than replacing the algorithm.

n=2048 cond=1 batch=8 (~7376us, 2nd-largest shape): the Householder path is device-STARVED -- 8 CTAs on 148 SMs, ~95% idle, latency-bound. cond=1 is MILD (cond(A)~10 -> Gram cond ~100, deep inside CholeskyQR's safe range, unlike the cond=2 that killed n=512). Convert it to batched CholeskyQR: pool the 8 matrices -> batched 3xTF32 SYRK Gram -> batched Cholesky (reuse your just-built gram_3xtf32 / batched_chol_upper / batched_chol_upper_fp64) -> TRSM for Q -> ORHR_COL reconstruct exact (H,tau). Default CholeskyQR2 (one refinement pass for orthogonality). Per-matrix guard on the FACTORIZATION itself (non-PD Cholesky OR post-reconstruct residual ||A-QR||/||A|| over tol -> geqrf demote), NOT on input cond, so held-out n=2048 mixed/ill-cond members stay correct. Budget the ORHR_COL reconstruct cost (it can land on the critical path); if batched SYRK at batch=8 underfills, pool into one concatenated GEMM. The n=4096 path already uses CholeskyQR successfully -- extend that proven approach down to n=2048. Branch off the clean baseline.

Ported the brief-0 kernels (gram_3xtf32/batched_chol_upper/batched_chol_upper_fp64) and built a batched CholeskyQR for n=2048 B>=4: Ozaki INT8 EXACT Gram (cond(G)~5e9 needs it -- the manager's 'cond~10 mild' premise is WRONG, measured cond(A)~1.6e4-6.8e4) -> FP64 DMMA blocked Cholesky -> 3xTF32 TRSM -> orhr_col + tau-override + per-matrix factorization gate (non-PD OR Q-colnorm-off-unit -> geqrf demote, NOT input cond). VALID all guards (diff guard's reseeded n2048 mixed/rankdef pass via the gate). shape5 = 12917us vs ~7376 baseline (1.75x REGRESSION); geomean 1838. nsys: the FP64 Cholesky dominates (~42%): diag kernel 15.6%/3.9ms (latency-bound, 8 CTAs, 64 barriers/panel x 32 panels), FP64 DMMA trailing 17%/4.3ms (underutilized at B=8 -- late-panel GEMMs underfill, ~7.5x off DMMA peak), panel solve 9.7%. Gram ~7%, TRSM ~15%. Next: attack the FP64 Cholesky -- try cuSOLVER batched potrf, or larger panel width to fill the trailing, or cut sequential-panel latency.

FINAL n2048 CholeskyQR candidate (one-level FP64 blocked chol). Added + measured a two-level FP64 Cholesky (fat k=256 outer trailing GEMM) to test the manager's device-fill hypothesis: the fat trailing DID improve device fill (trailing 4.3->3ms, the k=256 d884gemm hits ~270us/8 outer panels) BUT the wide panel solve added ~1.2ms of extra latency-bound chol_panel_solve launches -> NET TIED (12961 vs 12917). Kept one-level (simpler, flag off). VALID all guards. shape5 = 12925us vs 7376 baseline (1.75x REGRESSION); geomean 1839. Final nsys: chol_diag_smem_fp64 15.6%/3.9ms (latency-bound: 8 CTAs do a sequential O(64^3) FP64 Cholesky per panel x 32 panels, 95% device idle) + chol_panel_solve 9.7%/2.4ms (also latency-bound at B=8) = ~6.3ms of latency-bound per-matrix FP64 work that CANNOT be device-filled at B=8; trailing 9.9%, Ozaki Gram ~7%, TRSM ~15%, recon ~10%.

BRIEF EXHAUSTED -- NEGATIVE VERDICT (committed, validated, mild 1.75x regression). Built the full batched CholeskyQR for n=2048 B=8 (Ozaki INT8 EXACT Gram + custom FP64 DMMA blocked Cholesky [one-level AND a two-level fat-trailing variant] + 3xTF32 TRSM + orhr_col + tau-override + per-matrix FACTORIZATION gate -> geqrf demote). ALL GUARDS PASS. shape5 = 12925us vs ~7376 baseline (1.75x slower); geomean 1839 vs 1756. TWO MANAGER PREMISES TESTED: (1) 'cond=1 is mild (cond~10)' -- FALSE, measured cond(A)~1.6e4-6.8e4 -> cond(G)~5e9 (cond is a dynamic-range knob, not a condition number); this forces an EXACT Gram + FP64 Cholesky, the SAME tax that killed n=512. (2) 'Householder device-starved at B=8 so CholeskyQR wins' -- the starvation is REAL (baseline = 69% panel_factor + 14% Minv, latency-bound on ~8 CTAs) BUT CholeskyQR's FP64 Cholesky is ALSO latency-bound at B=8: nsys shows chol_diag 15.6%/3.9ms + chol_panel_solve 9.7%/2.4ms = ~6.3ms of sequential per-matrix O(64^3) FP64 work on 8 CTAs (95% device idle) -- it cannot be device-filled either, so it just trades Householder's latency for its own. DEVICE-FILL CONFIRMED PER YOUR ASK: the two-level fat k=256 trailing GEMM DID cut the trailing 4.3->3ms (better fill), but the wide panel solve added ~1.2ms latency-bound launches -> net tied. Tried: cuSOLVER batched FP64 potrf (18.2ms, WORSE), warp-sync diagonal (worse -- the diag is compute/smem-bound not barrier-bound). VERDICT: CholeskyQR loses at n=2048 B=8. THE KEY ACTIONABLE INSIGHT (crossover): CholeskyQR wins where Householder is SEVERELY device-starved AND the batched FP64 Cholesky has enough matrices to fill -- that is the n=4096 B=2 regime (already on CholeskyQR). At n=2048 B=8 the Householder starvation is milder (7.4ms) and the FP64 Cholesky is itself starved, so the crossover has flipped. RECOMMENDATION: do not pursue CholeskyQR for n2048; the FP64 latency floor at B=8 is fundamental. To attack n2048's 7.4ms, the real lever is the FP16 Householder panel_factor itself (69%, latency-bound) -- e.g. a coop/persistent panel that spreads the 8 matrices' panel work across more SMs, NOT an algorithm swap. Reusable artifacts now on this branch: batched_chol_upper_fp64_2lev (two-level fat-trailing FP64 DMMA Cholesky), plus the brief-0 kernels.

n=512 panel_factor RECURSIVE within-panel blocking to shrink the serial barrier chain. All three workers converged: the per-column Householder panel_factor (1 __syncthreads/column) is the universal latency/barrier bottleneck that starves the already-WMMA trailing apply (tensor cores 99% idle on n=512). The trailing update and compact-WY build_Minv are ALREADY on tensor cores -- the untried lever is the PANEL's own critical path. Recursively block the OB=64 panel: factor it as two OB=32 (or four OB=16) sub-panels, fully factoring sub-panel 1 (a shorter serial chain), applying its compact-WY block reflector to sub-panel 2 via WMMA (tensor-core, not serial), then factoring sub-panel 2 -- so the longest serial-__syncthreads sub-chain halves while the cross-sub-panel update runs on idle tensor cores. This raises the tensor-core/serial work ratio and shortens the barrier-bound critical path on the device-FULL n=512 (batch=640). Profile with ncu to confirm panel barrier-stall% drops and tensor pipe-active% rises. Keep the FP16 algorithm + the OB=64 outer geometry as the panel's external contract (recurse INSIDE it). Decorrelated from W1 (n1024 TSQR row-split) and W2 (n512 occupancy). Branch off the clean baseline. This generalizes to n=1024/2048/4096 if it lands.

Implemented the brief's recursive within-panel blocking in the standalone cm-OV panel (b=64): factor sub-panel 1 (cols 0..31, bulk only <32) -> WMMA cross-update C2<-(I-V1 T1 V1^T)C2 (S1=V1^TV1, T1^T fwd-sub, W=V1^TC2, Y=T1^TW, C2-=V1Y, all nvcuda::wmma) -> factor sub-panel 2. CORRECT: all guards CLEAN incl the B=640 diff guard (the WMMA cross-update reproduces the factorization exactly -- a real correctness milestone). RESULT NEUTRAL: panel_factor unchanged (9.9->10.1%), geomean 1750.9 vs 1756 (within noise). ncu confirms the panel's LSU+latency profile is unchanged (48% occ, 30% no-eligible-warp, 11 warp-cyc/inst, Mem Pipes 41%). ROOT CAUSE the win didn't land: the cross-update's OWN overhead cancels the rank-1 bulk it removes -- the T1 forward-sub is an O(HB^3) serial chain (32 threads, sequential in i), plus ~6 added barriers, plus FP16 staging of V1/C2 (the FP32 panel can't feed WMMA directly). Next: cut the cross-update overhead (cheaper T1, fewer barriers) or apply to PAF's PHASE P (the 50.8% kernel) -- but PAF factors IB=16 panels (shorter chains, less upside) and is high-risk.

FINAL: recursive within-panel blocking (correct, all guards CLEAN) is NEUTRAL (geomean 1754.8 vs 1756.07, within noise). Tested an m-gate (only recurse large-m panels where the cross-update fixed overhead is amortized) -- also neutral/slightly worse. nsys: panel_factor cm-OV unchanged at 10.2% (~320us). ncu (vs baseline): panel LSU/latency/occupancy profile UNCHANGED (48% occ, 30% no-eligible-warp, 11 warp-cyc/inst, Mem Pipes 41%, ALU 39.5%/LSU 42%). ROOT CAUSE the brief's lever doesn't land (firmly pinned): the panel's critical path is WARP-0's SERIAL LOOK-AHEAD reflector chain (b=64 sequential reflector computes, each data-dependent on the prior column), NOT the O(m*b^2) rank-1 bulk. The bulk (warps 1-7) is ALREADY overlapped behind warp-0's look-ahead, so moving the cross-sub-panel coupling to WMMA frees a pipe that was idle anyway AND inserts a SERIAL cross-update (T1 forward-sub + WMMA + ~6 barriers) INTO warp-0's critical path -> net longer, hence neutral-to-worse. Also: the FP32-smem panel forces FP16 staging of V1/C2 for the WMMA (the staging LSU ~cancels the rank-1 saved).

BRIEF EXHAUSTED -- recursion BUILT + CORRECT, but NEUTRAL (committed; geomean 1754.8 vs baseline 1756.07, within noise). I implemented the brief faithfully: recursive 2x32 within-panel blocking in the standalone OB=64 cm-OV panel -- factor sub-panel 1 (per-column, bulk only <32) -> WMMA cross-update C2<-(I-V1 T1 V1^T)C2 (S1=V1^TV1, T1^T forward-sub, W=V1^TC2, Y=T1^TW, C2-=V1Y, all nvcuda::wmma) -> factor sub-panel 2. The WMMA cross-update reproduces the factorization EXACTLY (all guards CLEAN incl the B=640 diff guard -- a real correctness win for the kernel toolbox: batched_chol etc. + now a verified in-panel WY block-apply). BUT it does not speed up the panel: nsys panel_factor unchanged (9.9->10.2%), ncu profile unchanged (48% occ, 30% no-eligible-warp, 11 warp-cyc/inst). ROOT CAUSE FOUND (refines the brief's hypothesis -- this is the load-bearing finding): the n=512 panel's critical path is NOT the rank-1 bulk -- it is WARP-0's SERIAL LOOK-AHEAD reflector chain (b sequential reflector computes, each data-dependent on the previous column's update). The bulk (warps 1-7) is ALREADY fully overlapped behind warp-0's look-ahead (the kernel is warp-specialized exactly for this). So recursive blocking (a) frees the tensor pipe which was idle but uncontended, and (b) INSERTS a serial cross-update (T1 forward-sub O(HB^3) + WMMA + ~6 barriers) straight into warp-0's critical path -> net neutral-to-worse. Secondary: the FP32-smem panel forces FP16 staging of V1/C2 for WMMA, whose LSU ~cancels the rank-1 it removes. WHAT WOULD ACTUALLY WIN (recommend redirecting): shorten WARP-0's look-ahead chain, not the bulk. The PAF kernel ALREADY has this lever -- g_paf_help (pivot-cooperation: HELP warps split warp-0's next-pivot m-pass) -- but it is set to 1 (OFF) for n512 because 'the m<=512 panel m-pass is SHORT and occupancy-rich'. For the STANDALONE cm-OV panel (9.9%, which has NO pivot-coop), adding HELP-warp look-ahead splitting could cut its warp-0 chain. OR: make the panel FP16-smem (half8, like the n2048 cm_coop_h variant) -> 2x occupancy (fixes the 48% cap) AND lets WMMA read V1/C2 with zero staging -- THEN recursion might pay. Both are larger changes decorrelated from this brief. NET: the panel is at its warp-0-look-ahead wall; the rank-1 bulk (the brief's target) is not the bottleneck. The cm-OV panel is only 9.9% anyway -- the big 50.8% is qr_panel_apply_fused (already WMMA, near roofline).

n=1024 dense (3 of 12 shapes ~3588us; second-largest dominant cluster) trailing-update PRECISION push to FP8, as a SECOND independent shot at the FP8 lever (W1 takes n=512 dense). FP8 is the only lever with a sub-1000us ceiling, so buy two shots that clear the gate by DIFFERENT correction mechanisms. Recast the n=1024 trailing-reflector apply A2 -= V*(T^T*(V^T*A2)) as an FP8 E4M3 tensor-core GEMM (E4M3 not E5M2 -- mantissa matters more than range for the factor gate; FP32 accumulate). Clear the FP32 gate via ITERATIVE RESIDUAL REFINEMENT (GEMM-refinement): compute the residual delta = (exact apply) - (FP8 apply) in FP16, then a second FP8 block-GEMM on the residual to recover the lost low-order bits -- a different correction than W1's Newton-Schulz re-orthogonalization, so the two FP8 shots fail/succeed for different reasons and we learn WHICH correction clears the gate. Gate by a per-matrix conditioning probe with FP16 fallback for ill-cond members. Different shape than W1 (no file collision). The existing kernel has NO FP8 path (only a stale 'FP8 far worse' comment about build_Minv, a different use -- retest it). Validate factor+orth on dense+mixed+nearrank. Branch off the clean baseline. If W1's gate clears first, this still banks the n=1024 half of the geomean win.

Built the full FP8 E4M3 trailing-apply with 3-term GEMM-refinement (the brief's exact correction: bf16->FP8 hi/lo split, V transposed for the FP8-required TN layout, gemm_fp8 helper, C-=Vt^T(Yhi+Ylo)+Vtlo^T Yhi). TWO build-and-measured blockers, FP8 left OFF: (1) cublasGemmStridedBatchedEx with FP8 E4M3 returns CUBLAS_STATUS_NOT_SUPPORTED (status=7) -- FIRST on the native NN apply layout, then AGAIN after transposing V to FP8's required TN (transa=T,transb=N); FP8 GemmEx imposes further alignment/dimension/scale constraints the variable-(m,rest) apply violates -> a working FP8 apply needs cublasLt + explicit scale factors + the transpose, a large rewrite whose overhead negates FP8's ~2x rate. (2) DECISIVE: fresh ncu on the n1024 apply kernel (qr_panel_apply_fused, 41.8%) shows it is LATENCY-bound by the PHASE-P panel -- 19% compute, 0.77% DRAM, 51% no-eligible-warp, 16 warp-cyc/inst -- NOT compute/memory bound. So the trailing GEMM is not the n1024 bottleneck (the panel's warp-0 serial look-ahead is, per brief-2; paf_help=2/ov_coop=2 already split it), and FP8 on the apply cannot speed up n1024 even if the layout worked. The 3-term refinement IS ~FP16-equivalent precision (would clear the factor gate like the existing FP16 path), so the CORRECTION mechanism is sound -- it is the FP8 GEMM API + the bottleneck location that block n1024. geomean 1754.98 (FP8 off). All guards CLEAN.

BRIEF EXHAUSTED -- FP8-on-n1024-trailing is a NO-GO, two independent build-and-measured grounds (committed, FP8 machinery present but disabled, geomean 1755 = baseline; all guards CLEAN). I built the brief's EXACT correction: FP8 E4M3 3-term GEMM-refinement on C-=V*Y (bf16->FP8 hi/lo split, V transposed to FP8's required TN layout, gemm_fp8, C-=Vt^T Yhi + Vt^T Ylo + Vtlo^T Yhi). FINDINGS: (1) cublasGemmStridedBatchedEx with FP8 E4M3 returns CUBLAS_STATUS_NOT_SUPPORTED (status=7) -- measured TWICE: on the apply's native NN layout, and AGAIN after the TN transpose. FP8 GemmEx imposes further alignment/dimension/scale constraints the variable-(m,rest) apply GEMMs violate. A working FP8 apply needs cublasLt + explicit A/B scale pointers + the data transpose -- a large rewrite whose transpose+scale overhead negates FP8's ~2x compute rate. (2) DECISIVE and the more important finding: fresh ncu on the n1024 apply kernel (qr_panel_apply_fused = 41.8% of n1024) shows it is LATENCY-BOUND by the fused PHASE-P panel, NOT compute/memory-bound: 19% SM compute, 0.77% DRAM, 51% no-eligible-warp, 16 warp-cyc/inst. The trailing GEMM is therefore NOT the n1024 bottleneck -- the panel's warp-0 serial look-ahead is (consistent with my brief-2 verdict), and the n1024 regime ALREADY applies the only panel levers that exist (paf_help=2, ov_coop=2 pivot-cooperation). So FP8 on the trailing apply cannot improve n1024's geomean even if the GEMM API allowed it. NOTE on the correction mechanism (the manager's learning goal, vs W1's Newton-Schulz): the 3-term FP8 GEMM-refinement IS ~FP16-equivalent precision and WOULD clear the n1024 factor gate (2.44e-3) -- the same as the existing FP16 apply that already passes -- so the CORRECTION is sound; it is the FP8 GEMM API + the bottleneck location that kill n1024, not the refinement math. CROSS-CUTTING RECOMMENDATION (spans my 3 briefs): the entire large-n family (n512/n1024/n2048) is bottlenecked by the PANEL's warp-0 serial look-ahead reflector chain, NOT the trailing GEMM. For n1024 specifically the apply is only ~21% (outer nvjet) + a latency-bound fused kernel. W1 should CHECK whether n512's apply is genuinely compute-bound (where FP8 could help) or also panel-bound like n1024 -- if n512's qr_panel_apply is also latency-bound, the fleet's FP8 pivot needs rethinking. If FP8 IS pursued, it must go through cublasLt (scale factors) and target a shape whose apply is provably compute-bound by ncu first.

n=2048 b8 (7376us, device 95% idle): dissolve the SERIAL PANEL via PANEL-LEVEL CholeskyQR2+ORHR_COL. Your own finding said whole-matrix CholeskyQR dies (cond(A)~1e4 -> Gram cond~5e9 forbids TF32). BUT the key insight: a SINGLE PANEL is only b=32 columns wide, and a narrow contiguous 32-col slice of a cond-1e4 matrix has MILD conditioning (cond typically <100) -- so per-PANEL CholeskyQR2 is FP32/3xTF32-safe where whole-matrix is not. Replace the serial panel_factor_smem_wsp_cmf chain (the O(b) per-column __syncthreads warp-0 look-ahead, the latency wall) with: per-panel Gram S=V^T V (one tensor-core GEMM), b x b Cholesky in smem (one CTA, O(1) sync depth), Q=V R^-1 (TRSM/GEMM), ONE reorthogonalization pass (CQR2), then reconstruct that panel's compact (H,tau) via the EXISTING _reconstruct_householder / orhr_col machinery (lines 6385/6402) WITH the tau-from-V override (line 6272) that already passes the gate at n4096. Keep the existing blocked TF32 trailing update. This swaps O(b) serial syncs for ~3 tensor-core GEMMs -- the panel becomes tensor-core-bound on a device that is currently 95% idle. Reuse the n>=4096 ORHR code, generalize/gate it to n=2048. Profile to confirm panel barrier-stall drops + tensor-active rises.
